domain_description: Reading, writing, and thinking skills that transfer across subjects — strategy instruction that builds comprehension, scaffolds that make complex texts and disciplinary writing accessible, and protocols that teach students to evaluate sources, deconstruct media, and design tasks worth thinking hard about. All interventions cross-referenced to peer-reviewed meta-analyses where one exists.

skills.description: Pick the right reading comprehension strategy for the text and the class — reciprocal teaching, summarisation, prediction, questioning, text structure mapping, monitoring — and combine them so students have a small, well-rehearsed toolkit instead of a long list of one-off tricks.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Reading comprehension strategies strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: EEF rates this Very low. Teachers need PD on a small set of strategies (reciprocal teaching, summarisation, prediction, monitoring), but no materials change and no structural reorganisation. The harder part is fidelity over time — strategies have to be modelled, practised, then released to students gradually — not the up-front investment.

skills.description: Analyse what makes a text hard for your students — vocabulary, sentence structure, background knowledge, text structure — and design targeted scaffolds (pre-teaching, graphic organisers, signal-word work, chunking) so students can climb a challenging text instead of being filtered out by it.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Reading comprehension strategies strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Teachers need PD in recognising text structures (cause-effect, compare-contrast, problem-solution), signal-words, and how to design graphic organisers and pre-teaching that fit the specific text. No materials cost but real lesson-design work — and Bogaerds-Hazenberg's delayed-posttest finding (effects faded without sustained practice) means scaffolds have to be revisited across the year, not deployed once.

skills.description: Design discipline-specific writing scaffolds — Toulmin for argument, CER (claim-evidence-reasoning) for science, IMRAD for lab reports, narrative arc for English — so students learn the genre conventions of each subject, not just generic 'good writing' that lands nowhere.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Teachers need to know their discipline's genre conventions (different for science, history, English), model them, and embed scaffolds into existing writing tasks. Higher PD lift than reciprocal teaching because scaffolds must be discipline-specific, but no materials cost. Sustained PD matters — scaffolds work when teachers can model the discipline's reasoning, not just supply a template.
